Training/Assessment preparation
KNOW THE STANDARD

Assessment preparation

A published standard is a target, not a training plan. Find out what your test actually includes, build the parts you are missing and practise under similar conditions.

01

Start with the real requirements

Use the publisher’s current instructions for activities, equipment, permitted rest, scoring, and any deadlines. Check the full instructions before setting your training targets.

  • Check if requirements vary by role, age or application route.
  • Record a starting result for each event.
  • Track the gap between your starting point and your target.
02

Train the whole test

If a selection test includes rucking, strength, running and swimming, leaving one part to chance is a poor strategy.

  • Prioritise your weakest relevant component without ignoring the others.
  • Practise transitions, equipment and timing where the rules allow.
  • Schedule a rehearsal, then leave time to recover and adjust.
03

Make a plan you can sustain

Build towards demanding work, but keep enough recovery to actually improve.

  • Alternate harder sessions and more manageable sessions.
  • Increase work gradually instead of chasing arbitrary pack weights.
  • Recheck current official requirements before the actual assessment.

Prepare for your specific test

Choose the programme to review its published components and preparation priorities. The organiser sets the actual standards.

PFQ

  • 800 m run
  • 400 m run carrying weights
  • Burpees for 3 minutes
  • Squats for 2 minutes
  • Strict pull-ups for 1 minute

Preparation priorities

  • Record each timed event separately; use the prescribed technique, order and rest.
  • Combine controlled running intervals and bodyweight work; rehearse the test format after building repeatability.
